shorts.title: Judge to Trump: "I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees." #Shorts
shorts.hook: A judge on Trump's golf course trees
shorts.narration: [deadpan] A federal judge just wrote, in a ruling, "I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees." [beat] Then she spoke for the trees anyway. Judge Ana Reyes blocked the Trump administration from removing trees at a D.C. golf course, after the government took down more than 430 of them in one day. [sarcastic] She noted the notice came at 4:55 on the Friday of a holiday weekend. [beat] Nothing says transparency like a Friday-night chainsaw. Trump called the ruling unconstitutional and says he'll appeal. [incredulous] The leader of the free world is fighting a legal war over a golf course. [beat] The Constitution puts the judicial power in the courts. Not in the greenskeeper. Out here in California, we hug trees. Trump fans, when a judge says follow the rules, which part of that do you find woke? Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

shorts.title: Trump: "I am thinking about moving the Press" — after denying a pool #Shorts
shorts.hook: Trump: no pool, just evict the press
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Trump on Truth Social: "I am not building a swimming pool in the White House Briefing Room." [beat] Great start. Then, same post: "I am thinking about moving the Press, and putting them in a different location." [sarcastic] So, no pool. Just an eviction. The New York Times reported on October 20 that Trump had discussed replacing the briefing room with an indoor pool, which he denies. [beat] Denial, then eviction. A bold new model of transparency. The day before, he wrote that he may move the "Fake News to a less obnoxious location." [incredulous] Friends, the First Amendment says no law abridging "the freedom of speech, or of the press." [beat] Technically a moving van isn't a law. Scary logic, though. What exactly is a president afraid of in a room full of questions? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

shorts.title: Trump on Comey: "I know nothing about it" — DOJ moves to charge him a 3rd time #Shorts
shorts.hook: DOJ goes after Comey a third time
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Asked about James Comey, Trump said: "I think he's a dirty cop, James Comey, but I know nothing about it." [beat] Strong opinion, zero information. Now the Justice Department has taken steps to charge Comey a third time, with two Espionage Act counts over a 2016 New York Times story. Prosecutors allege a leak; Comey denies it. No grand jury indicted him. The DOJ filed a criminal information, which it says preserves the statute of limitations. [incredulous] His first indictment was dismissed because the prosecutor was improperly appointed. Former Justice Department inspector general Michael Bromwich called this one, quote, "absolutely bizarro world stuff." [beat] Article II says the president shall take care that the laws be faithfully executed. Faithfully. Not repeatedly, until one sticks. MAGA friends, if the case is so strong, why does it need three tries? Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

shorts.title: Trump: oil firms are "making hundreds of billions of dollars" — his stocks too #Shorts
shorts.hook: Trump's oil stocks and the Iran war
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Trump says U.S. oil companies are "making hundreds of billions of dollars." [beat] He would know. A report by Democrats on Congress's Joint Economic Committee, obtained by CBS News, says Trump's oil and gas holdings are now worth between 22.5 and 81.6 million dollars, up from 12.6 to 46 million at the end of 2025. The report says his accounts sold up to a million dollars of Exxon stock the day he announced an Iran ceasefire. The White House says it's independently managed and, quote, "There are no conflicts of interest." [sarcastic] Sure. [beat] Democrats estimate families paid about 856 dollars more for gas since the war began. The Constitution's preamble promises to promote the general Welfare. [beat] It never says the general portfolio. Republicans, if a Democrat's stocks soared in a war, would you call it a conflict? Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

shorts.title: Judge on Trump DOJ: "sweeping and unprecedented theory of executive authority" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Judge slaps down DOJ's firing theory
shorts.narration: [deadpan] A federal judge just called the Trump Justice Department's argument a "sweeping and unprecedented theory of executive authority." [beat] Judge Jesse Furman ruled that DOJ unlawfully fired prosecutor Maurene Comey, and reinstated her retroactively with back pay. The government admitted she got "outstanding" ratings from 2019 through 2024. [sarcastic] So the firing was not about performance. [beat] The administration cited Article II, which is the legal version of, because I said so. Furman said accepting that would "unsettle the very equilibrium established by this Nation's constitutional system." Her lawsuit alleges she was probably fired because Trump dislikes her father. The Justice Department says it will appeal. [incredulous] The Declaration of Independence says of King George: "He has obstructed the Administration of Justice." [beat] Different century, same complaint. MAGA friends, who exactly is the DOJ working for? Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.
